title: Construction and local exactness of the full Cech sheaf complex
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and
$(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an open cover. For $p\geq0$ and $y:\{0,\ldots,p\}\to I$ put
$U_y=\bigcap_l U_{y(l)}$ and write $j_y:U_y\to X$. There exist an augmented complex
$\epsilon:\mathcal F[0]\to D^\bullet$ and identifications of the underlying module
presheaves of $D^p$ with $V\mapsto\prod_y\mathcal F(U_y\cap V)$, intertwining the
usual alternating face differentials. Under these identifications each coordinate
of the degree-zero augmentation is restriction $\mathcal F(V)\to\mathcal F(U_y\cap V)$.
Moreover $D^p\cong\prod_y j_{y,*}(\mathcal F|_{U_y})$ and $\epsilon$ is a
quasi-isomorphism. This is the full complex with repeated indices, without any
bounded-above assertion or any assertion about a morphism out of $X$.

proof.text: Apply the construction theorem, which needs no covering hypothesis, obtaining D, epsilon, the sectionwise isomorphisms, their differential and augmentation laws, and the open-direct-image term isomorphisms.
Apply the local Cech quasi-isomorphism theorem to this D and epsilon, using its differential and augmentation laws, separately for each cover member.

Globalize in each homology degree. Restriction preserves limits by the existing proved instance Scheme.Modules.preservesLimitsOfSize_restrictFunctor in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.QuasicoherentKernel; it preserves colimits by the restriction/direct-image adjunction. Hence it commutes with short-complex homology. Naturality of the homology comparison isomorphisms identifies restriction of the global homology map with the local homology maps, which are isomorphisms. A module-sheaf map invertible on the cover is globally invertible: local monomorphisms imply a global monomorphism, while its cokernel restricts to zero and vanishing on an open cover implies that cokernel is zero. Therefore every homology map is invertible and epsilon is a quasi-isomorphism. This argument also works for an empty cover of the empty scheme. The Lean module proves all this globalization explicitly in private helpers.

theorem exists_cech_sheaf_resolution
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤)
    (F : X.Modules) :
    ∃ (D : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ)
      (ε : (CochainComplex.single₀ X.Modules).obj F ⟶ D)
      (e : ∀ p : ℕ, (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).obj
          (D.X p).val ≅
        ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
          ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).X p),
      (∀ p : ℕ,
        (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            (D.d p (p + 1)).val ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
            ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).d p (p + 1)) ∧
      (∀ (y : Fin 1 → ι) (V : X.Opens),
        ((PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            ((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 F).inv ≫ ε.f 0).val ≫
          (e 0).hom ≫
            Pi.π (fun y : Fin 1 → ι =>
              ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
                (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat).obj
                  (op (∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)))) y).app (op V) =
          F.presheafModuleCat.map (prod.snd : (∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)) ⨯ V ⟶ V).op) ∧
      (∀ p : ℕ, Nonempty (D.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ fun y : Fin (p + 1) → ι =>
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (⨅ l, U (y l)).ι).obj (F.restrict (⨅ l, U (y l)).ι))) ∧
      QuasiIso ε
